## Independent AI review — advisory (DR-033 §6)

**Reviewer** verdict:
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: The new link check itself is correct, but when it finds no link the PR still gets auto-merged. The label it applies promises "auto-merge withheld" and nothing withholds it, so the issue still stays open after the merge.
findings:
- blocking scripts/dispatch-issue.sh:1071-1077 (step 6a) → 1093-1134 (step 6b) — When the link is not confirmed, step 6a labels the PR `needs-human-review` and posts a comment, but it sets no hold. Step 6b then runs `native_automerge_enabled` → `autonomy_may_merge` → `gh pr merge --squash --auto` exactly as before, and none of those steps read that label. The `ready-to-merge` workflow doesn't read it either (grep of .github/workflows shows only ai-review.yml and ai-review-retry.yml touch it). So the #2228 failure still happens end to end: the PR auto-merges on ai-review:pas…
- minor scripts/dispatch-issue.sh:1070-1072 — The readback runs immediately after `gh pr create`. If GitHub fills in `closingIssuesReferences` asynchronously (I believe it is usually synchronous, unverified), every fresh PR would be flagged by mistake. Consider a short bounded re-poll, e.g. 2-3 tries a few seconds apart, before declaring the link missing. That makes a false alarm less likely without turning a real failure into a silent pass.
- minor packages/minspec/tests/dispatch-issue-closing-link-verify.test.ts:129-137 — The ordering test only proves that the text `issue_linked_in_closing_refs "$ISSUE"` appears before the text `6b. Native auto-merge`. It would still pass if the verification had no effect on 6b at all, and today it has none. This is the pass-without-the-feature test shape; once the hold is wired, assert on the gate itself.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

**Security** verdict:
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: No security issues found. The change adds a read-only check that confirms each dispatched PR is actually linked to its issue, with no injection, secret or dependency risk. Three low-severity robustness notes, none blocking.
findings:
- LOW scripts/dispatch-issue.sh:1073-1077 — The new `needs-human-review` label does not hold the merge. On an unlinked PR, the check applies the label, then step 6b still arms native auto-merge whenever `native_automerge_enabled` is on. The ready-to-merge workflow does not read this label. So the PR can merge and leave the issue open, which is the failure #2228 describes. The comment and warning keep it visible, so invariant 2 (no silent gate) holds. But the label reads as a hold when it is not one, and the test title 'runs BEFORE native…
- LOW scripts/dispatch-issue.sh:1071 — The check reads `closingIssuesReferences` right after `gh pr create`. If GitHub fills in that field a moment after creation, a freshly created PR could be flagged as unlinked when it is fine (unverified). That would train humans to ignore the label. Recommendation: retry briefly with a delay before flagging, and make any wait long enough to cover the parse.
- INFO scripts/dispatch-issue.sh:1075 — The comment is not idempotent: every re-dispatch of the same branch posts another copy. It also always says 'This PR carries a `Closes #N` trailer'. When the PR already existed and was reused, `$BODY` was never written to it, so that sentence may be false. Recommendation: check for an existing marker before posting, as the shepherd hand-off does with SHEPHERD_HANDOFF_MARKER, and drop the claim about the trailer. Injection check: the printf format string is a fixed single-quoted literal and `$IS…
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Reviewer agent is read-only and credential-free; verdict enforced by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`review-decide.sh`). Advisory only — the human holds the merge keystroke (never-wrong / HITL)._

commits.messageBody:
… text

#1322 made the dispatcher WRITE a deterministic `Closes #$ISSUE` trailer into
every auto-dispatched PR body, so closure no longer depended on the agent
spontaneously writing a GitHub keyword. #2228 found that stopped being enough:
PRs opened after ~05:20Z on 2026-09-30 carried the trailer verbatim yet
GitHub reported `closingIssuesReferences` EMPTY, so merging them would not
have auto-closed their issues. The external trigger for that is unverified (a
GitHub-side incident/behaviour change is the lead candidate, per the issue,
and this session has no network access to confirm it).

Root cause: the pipeline WRITES the Closes trailer and trusts GitHub's
keyword parser to act on it, but nothing anywhere reads that parse back to
confirm it worked — a required outcome (merge closes the issue) rested on a
single unwitnessed producer, which is exactly what constitution invariant 2
forbids ("no required check hinges on a single producer that one
permission/config gap can disable — provide an independent second witness").
That gap exists regardless of what triggers a given failure to link, so it is
fixed here independently of the still-unverified external cause.

Adds `issue_linked_in_closing_refs` (pure, exposed via the `--issue-linked`
seam) and wires it into `run_reviewer_stage()` right after the PR is
confirmed to exist: read `closingIssuesReferences` back via `gh pr view`,
and if the target issue is not in it, fail VISIBLY — label the PR
`needs-human-review` and post an explanatory comment — instead of silently
proceeding. Fails closed on a read error exactly like the sibling diff
enumeration check: an API failure is treated the same as "not confirmed
linked", never as "assume it worked".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
The Security reviewer on #2294 (verify Closes-trailer PRs actually link)
blocked because the new witness did not hold anything. Step 6a labelled an
unconfirmed link needs-human-review and commented, then 6b armed
gh pr merge --auto regardless. So the #2228-shaped PR still merged itself
the moment ready-to-merge went green, and left its issue open.

Root cause: 6a's result never reached 6b. The --auto arm reads no label,
and ready-to-merge holds only on hold:*, changes or an unverified pass, so
a needs-human-review label beside an armed merge withheld nothing. The only
test of the link was textual ("6a precedes 6b"), and ordering without a data
dependency blocks nothing.

6a now sets closing_link_confirmed. It starts at 0 and turns 1 only on a
positive match, so an API error still fails closed. 6b gains an elif,
inside the existing native_automerge_enabled guard with no new fi, that
withholds the arm and says why when the link is unconfirmed.

New T3 test: it drives the real 6a..6b span of run_reviewer_stage against a
stub gh that records every call, with a linked-case CONTROL. Red on the
pre-fix script: both "does NOT arm" cases failed because --auto was armed.
Green here; drain-selfheal plus all dispatch-* suites pass (13 files, 384
tests).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
